Kipferl 0.7.3 makes `kipferl add` work for more real packages and shows you
which packages have actually been tested. It also fixes a regular-expression gap
and adds a Nix install path.

## What is new

- **`kipferl deps verified`** lists the package versions and workflows that were
  tested against the exact runtime and platform of your binary. `--json` exports
  the evidence. It lists `tzdata`, checked through real installation, offline
  restore and a standalone binary run away from the source tree.
  `trove-classifiers` passed against the 0.7.2 runtime and is not listed.
- **Fewer false dependency failures.** `kipferl add` no longer stops on optional
  transitive requirements that cannot apply, such as test or docs extras whose
  markers prove them inactive. Requirements whose conditions are active or
  unclear are still rejected, and the original wheel metadata is kept.
- **Python octal escapes in regular expressions.** `re` now accepts null-prefixed
  and three-digit octal escapes such as `\0` and `\101` in search, findall,
  substitution and split. Numeric backreferences, short nonzero class escapes
  and surrogate patterns remain unsupported.
- **Nix.** `nix profile add github:niklas-heer/kipferl` builds the CLI from
  source. It tracks `main`, so it can be ahead of the latest release.
- **Package guide.** The website now has a workflow compatibility guide with
  Verified, Limited, Unsupported and Untested ratings, and a ranked list of the
  100 packages we want to support next.

## What this does not mean

Compiling a package is still not proof that it works. Only the workflows listed
by `kipferl deps verified` are tested, and only for the versions shown there.
The 1,000-package source audit from 0.7.2 is unchanged.

## Upgrade

Run `brew update && brew upgrade kipferl`, or download your platform's binary
and verify its adjacent checksum. `kipferl --version` reports `Kipferl v0.7.3`.

The embedded runtime changed (regex escapes), so runtime-bound dependency locks
may need refreshing: rerun `kipferl add` for your declared requirements, review
and commit the lock, then run your application tests. Never edit hashes to
bypass a mismatch. Standalone applications you built earlier keep running.

Package evidence: https://kipferl.dev/docs/guides/package-audit
